enums.name: ke_result_domain
enums.doc: The domains that own a range of result codes. A domain's own codes are written `KE_RESULT_CODE(KE_RESULT_DOMAIN_ <DOMAIN >, n)` in its header, with `n` from 1 up.

enums.name: ke_result
enums.doc: What a fallible call returns: `KE_OK`, or the code of the failure. The detail of a failure goes to the failing library's log, never into the code. A caller treats a code it does not know as `KE_RESULT_GENERAL`. Ignoring the result of a call is a compiler warning where the compiler supports it.

values.name: KE_VARIANT_ENTITY
values.doc: An entity of the world the component lives in: the only place a component holds one.

enums.name: ke_ecs_access
enums.doc: How a query term's column is used.

structs.name: ke_vec3
structs.doc: Three floats, x then y then z.

structs.name: ke_vec4
structs.doc: Four floats, x then y then z then w.

structs.name: ke_quat
structs.doc: A rotation; the four lanes are x, y, z, w.

structs.name: ke_transform
structs.doc: Spatial transform: where a thing is, how it is turned, and how big it is.

structs.name: ke_variant_table_entry
structs.doc: One authored key and its value. Whoever accepts the key sets `consumed`; the loader reports every entry left unclaimed.

structs.name: ke_component_field
structs.doc: One field of a component: where it lies, what a scene writes into it, and the names an integer field may be written as.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The name a scene writes the field by.

fields.name: default_value
fields.doc: What the field holds when nothing authors it. KE_VARIANT_NULL means the header declared no default and zero stands.

fields.name: enum_names
fields.doc: The names a scene may write for an integer field, in value order; a name stands for its index. None leaves the field numeric.

fields.name: enum_count
fields.doc: Entries in `enum_names`.

structs.name: ke_component_params
structs.doc: What a component type is registered with.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Unique component name.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: Bytes per entity; 0 registers a tag (no storage).

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc: A power of two for a sized component; ignored for a tag of size 0.

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: The type's field layout, normally its field table; copied with every name it reaches, so it only has to live for the call. NULL registers the size alone.

fields.name: field_count
fields.doc: Entries in `fields`; 0 when `fields` is NULL.

structs.name: ke_ecs_query_term
structs.doc: One component a query matches and hands a column of, and how the column is used.

fields.name: access
fields.doc: Read, write, or both.

structs.name: ke_ecs_query_desc
structs.doc: A query to register: the entities having every term's component and every `with` component, and none of the `without` components.

fields.name: terms
fields.doc: One column each, in this order.

fields.name: with
fields.doc: Required, handing no column.

fields.name: without
fields.doc: Excluded.

fields.name: track_changes
fields.doc: Each resolve reports which segments changed since this query's previous resolve; such a query is never shared with another registration of the same description.

structs.name: ke_ecs_segment
structs.doc: One archetype's slice of a query match: the matched entities, plus one column base pointer per query term in the order query_register received them, each aligned 1:1 with `entities`. A tag term's column is NULL. Pointers stay valid until the next structural change.

fields.name: entities
fields.doc: The entities this segment matched.

fields.name: columns
fields.doc: One base pointer per query term.

fields.name: changed
fields.doc: For a query tracking changes: never false when, since the query's previous resolve, an entity of the segment gained a component of one of its terms or had one written through a resolve or a command; it may be true without that, and is true on the first resolve. False for a query that does not track changes.

fields.name: matched
fields.doc: Per term, the component it matched: the pair a wildcard pair term matched, the term's own component otherwise.

structs.name: ke_ecs_config
structs.doc: The values an ECS is created with, whatever its implementation, each applied as given.

fields.name: reserved_id_capacity
fields.doc: How many ids entity_reserve may hand out before the world issues any of its own; entity_reserve fails as out of memory once they are spent. Raise it for a world whose systems spawn heavily.

structs.name: ke_module_targets
structs.doc: The standard schedules of a world and their sets, which a module attaches its systems to.

fields.name: startup
fields.doc: Runs once, before the first tick's other schedules.

fields.name: pre_update
fields.doc: Runs first in every tick.

fields.name: fixed
fields.doc: Runs once per fixed step.

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Runs after the fixed steps in every tick.

fields.name: shutdown
fields.doc: Runs once, when the loop shuts down.

fields.name: render
fields.doc: Runs over the render world once per extraction; NULL where there is none.

fields.name: startup_set
fields.doc: In startup.

fields.name: pre_update_set
fields.doc: In pre_update.

fields.name: fixed_pre_update_set
fields.doc: In fixed, first.

fields.name: fixed_update_set
fields.doc: In fixed, after fixed_pre_update_set.

fields.name: fixed_post_update_set
fields.doc: In fixed, after fixed_update_set.

fields.name: update_set
fields.doc: In update, first.

fields.name: post_update_set
fields.doc: In update, after update_set.

fields.name: shutdown_set
fields.doc: In shutdown.

fields.name: render_begin_set
fields.doc: In render, first: where the frame begins.

fields.name: render_prepare_set
fields.doc: In render, after render_begin_set: where uploads run and passes make what they hand to others.

fields.name: render_queue_set
fields.doc: In render, after render_prepare_set: where passes are declared.

fields.name: render_submit_set
fields.doc: In render, after render_queue_set: where the frame is executed and presented.

vtables.name: ke_completion
vtables.doc: Work that finishes once, with a result: a job, an asynchronous operation, a read, a run, a submission. Whoever received it releases it exactly once; a completion that another call borrowed as a dependency is released only after the work that depends on it completed.

slots.name: poll
slots.doc: Whether the work finished; callable from any thread.
slots.return_doc: true once the work finished.

params.name: out_result
params.doc: Receives what the work finished with, when it finished.

slots.name: wait
slots.doc: Blocks until the work finishes and returns what it finished with. Callable from the thread that created the system the completion came from, and from inside a job when the completion came from that job system.
slots.return_doc: What the work finished with; KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED, at once, from any other thread, where the completion is passed as a dependency instead.

slots.name: release
slots.doc: Gives the completion back; the pointer is invalid afterwards. The work itself is not stopped.

vtables.name: ke_ecs
vtables.doc: One world: entity lifetime, component storage and queries. The ids, components and queries of one ke_ecs mean nothing to another.

slots.name: entity_create
slots.doc: Creates a fresh entity with no components. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

params.name: out_entity
params.doc: Receives the entity; the null entity on failure.

slots.name: entity_destroy
slots.doc: Destroys an entity and all its components; an entity that is not alive is left alone. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for the null entity or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

slots.name: component_register
slots.doc: Registers a component type by name, or returns the existing id if already registered. A repeated name with the same size, alignment and layout answers the same id. A repeated name with another layout and a field table on both registrations migrates the data of every entity and singleton by field name: a field of the same name and type is copied, a new field takes the default of the table, a field that is gone is dropped; the id stays. Without field tables a different size or alignment is refused.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT when the params are missing, the alignment is not a power of two, or the type differs from the name's prior registration with no field table to migrate by, what disagrees being logged; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: params
params.doc: The name, size, alignment and field table of the type.

params.name: out_cid
params.doc: Receives the component's id; KE_COMPONENT_INVALID on failure.

slots.name: component_lookup
slots.doc: Looks up a previously registered component by name.
slots.return_doc: false if no component of that name is registered.

params.name: name
params.doc: Component name to find.

params.name: out_meta
params.doc: Receives the component's id, size, and field metadata.

slots.name: component_meta
slots.doc: Looks up a registered component by id.
slots.return_doc: false for the null or an unknown component.

params.name: out_meta
params.doc: Receives the component's id, size, and field metadata.

slots.name: component_add
slots.doc: Attaches a component to an entity: its storage is zeroed, then seeded with the defaults of the field table the component was registered with, on the first attach; an entity that already has the component keeps its storage unchanged. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an entity that is not alive, the null entity or component, or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

params.name: out_data
params.doc: Receives the storage, valid until the next structural change on this ecs; NULL for a tag, and on failure.

slots.name: component_remove
slots.doc: Detaches a component from an entity; an entity that is not alive is left alone. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for the null entity or component, or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

slots.name: component_get
slots.doc: Returns an entity's component storage, or NULL if it doesn't have that component. The pointer is valid until the next structural change on this ecs.

slots.name: component_size
slots.doc: Byte size of a registered component's element; 0 for a tag or unknown cid.

slots.name: component_field_write
slots.doc: Writes value into component at the place field describes, converted to the field's type: an integer and a float convert to each other, a boolean to an integer, and a vector widens or narrows to the field's width; a string is cut to the field's size and stays NUL-terminated.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a null argument, or for a value that does not convert to the field's type or a size the type cannot have, writing nothing.

params.name: component
params.doc: The component's memory.

params.name: field
params.doc: Where in the component, and of which type and size.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value to write.

slots.name: query_register
slots.doc: Registers a query. A description equal to one registered before answers the id it got then, unless it tracks changes.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for no terms, a term with no access or an unknown one, more terms and filters than the backend's queries hold, or a query the backend refuses, its reason logged; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The terms, the required and excluded components, and whether changes are tracked.

params.name: out_query
params.doc: Receives the query; KE_QUERY_INVALID on failure.

slots.name: query_resolve
slots.doc: Resolves a query into archetype segments. MUST run single-threaded, before a parallel wave; afterwards the segments are plain memory touching no backend state.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an unknown query, missing output arrays or a zero capacity, or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

params.name: out_segments
params.doc: Receives the matched segments.

params.name: max_segments
params.doc: Capacity of out_segments. Counts the columns of the query's written terms as written, for change tracking.

params.name: out_columns
params.doc: Backing store of the segments' columns: segment i's columns are the term_count entries starting at index i * term_count, term_count being that of the description the query was registered with.

params.name: out_matched
params.doc: Backing store of the segments' matched components, laid out as out_columns.

params.name: out_count
params.doc: Receives how many segments the query matches; above max_segments, out_segments holds only the first max_segments of them, and the others keep their changes for the next resolve; zero on failure.

slots.name: entity_reserve
slots.doc: Reserves an entity id, callable concurrently from any wave thread — the one entity operation that is. The id is usable immediately as a reference; the entity itself appears in the world when component_add first runs for it, at the wave barrier. An implementation may not satisfy this by forwarding to entity_create, which is single-threaded. The implementation may replace a reserved id when the commands recorded with it are applied, rewriting every ENTITY field that holds it; a caller does not rely on the number before then.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY when every id the implementation can reserve was handed out.

params.name: out_entity
params.doc: Receives the id; the null entity on failure.

slots.name: entity_materialize
slots.doc: Brings a reserved id into the world, so an entity that never receives a component still exists. Structural; single-threaded. A no-op for an id that is already alive or was never reserved.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for the null entity or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

slots.name: singleton_add
slots.doc: Gives the world one value of a component, matched by no query: its storage is zeroed, then seeded with the defaults of the component's field table, the first time; a singleton that exists keeps its storage. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for the null or an unknown component, or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

params.name: out_data
params.doc: Receives the storage, valid until the next structural change on this ecs; NULL for a tag, and on failure.

slots.name: singleton_get
slots.doc: Returns the world's value of a component, or NULL if it has none. The pointer is valid until the next structural change on this ecs.

slots.name: singleton_remove
slots.doc: Takes a component's value from the world; a component without one is left alone. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for the null component or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

slots.name: pair
slots.doc: The component id of a pair: relation applied to target. A pair is added, removed, read and queried as any component, holding the relation's storage. With KE_ENTITY_WILDCARD as target the id matches every pair of the relation, in a query term, a with or a without alone.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an unknown relation or the null target; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: out_cid
params.doc: Receives the pair's id; KE_COMPONENT_INVALID on failure.

slots.name: pair_parts
slots.doc: The relation and the target of a pair's id.
slots.return_doc: false for an id that is not a pair.

params.name: out_relation
params.doc: Receives the relation.

params.name: out_target
params.doc: Receives the target, KE_ENTITY_WILDCARD for a wildcard pair.

slots.name: removal_track
slots.doc: Starts remembering the entities that lose component, by removal or by being destroyed. Single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for the null or an unknown component; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: out_tracker
params.doc: Receives the tracker.

slots.name: removals
slots.doc: Hands out the entities that lost the tracker's component since the previous call, and forgets them. Single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an unknown tracker or a null output.

params.name: out_entities
params.doc: Receives the entities.

params.name: out_count
params.doc: Receives how many were lost; above capacity, the rest stay for the next call.

slots.name: entity_components
slots.doc: The components an entity has, pairs included.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an entity that is not alive or a null output.

params.name: out_cids
params.doc: Receives the components.

params.name: out_count
params.doc: Receives how many it has; above capacity only the first fit.

slots.name: components
slots.doc: The components registered in the world.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a null output.

params.name: out_cids
params.doc: Receives the components.

params.name: out_count
params.doc: Receives how many are registered; above capacity only the first fit.

slots.name: snapshot
slots.doc: Captures the world's entities and the values of the listed components and of their singletons. Single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an unknown component; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: components
params.doc: What the snapshot holds the values of.

params.name: out_snapshot
params.doc: Receives the snapshot, freed with snapshot_free.

slots.name: restore
slots.doc: Brings the world back to a snapshot: afterwards it behaves as when the snapshot was taken for its entities, the ids later creations receive, and the components and singletons the snapshot lists, and for nothing else. A handle a component holds comes back as the number it was. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a snapshot of another world; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

slots.name: snapshot_free
slots.doc: Frees a snapshot; a null one is ignored.

vtables.name: ke_ecs_commands
vtables.doc: A queue of structural mutations. Every operation records its intent and returns; none changes the world while it runs. The queue is applied, in the order the operations were recorded, by whoever owns it, and an operation's effect is not observable before then. A caller needing a change visible at once uses ke_ecs, which mutates immediately. Recording never touches the world, so these operations may be called while other code reads it. The queue is applied while nothing else runs. An implementation that cannot accept an operation returns its code, logs the reason, and leaves the queue unchanged: KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED in a phase that may not change structure, KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY when the queue cannot grow.

slots.name: spawn
slots.doc: Records the creation of an entity and answers the id it will have. The id can be named by later operations of this queue, and by any caller, at once; the entity itself exists once the queue is applied.

params.name: out_entity
params.doc: Receives the id; KE_ENTITY_INVALID on failure.

slots.name: attach
slots.doc: Records giving `entity` the component `cid`, initialised from `size` bytes of `data`. The bytes are copied, so the caller's buffer need not outlive the call. `size` must equal the registered size of `cid`, or be 0 to attach the component without copying bytes into it.
slots.return_doc: KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT, besides the codes above, when `size` is neither 0 nor the registered size of `cid`.

slots.name: detach
slots.doc: Records removing component `cid` from `entity`.

slots.name: despawn
slots.doc: Records destroying `entity`.

slots.name: defer
slots.doc: Records a structural operation for work the fixed verbs above cannot express. `fn` runs when the queue is applied, in order with the other operations. `user_size` bytes of `user` are copied, so the caller's buffer need not outlive the call.
slots.return_doc: KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT, besides the codes above, for a null `fn`.

vtables.name: ke_module
vtables.doc: A piece that fits into a world by registering its systems in the standard schedules.

slots.name: attach
slots.doc: Registers the module's systems in targets, whose schedules must outlive the attachment.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for null targets or a null schedule the module uses; KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED when the module is already attached; the code a schedule refused a system with, nothing left registered.

params.name: targets
params.doc: Read during the call.

slots.name: detach
slots.doc: Removes exactly what attach registered, and nothing else: components and entities stay in the world. A module not attached is left alone.

callbacks.name: ke_defer_fn
callbacks.doc: A structural operation applied when the queue holding it is drained. `user` points at the copy of the payload passed to defer; `ecs` is the live world. A failure is returned, and the queue stops there: the operations recorded after it are dropped.

callbacks.name: ke_schedule_execute_fn
callbacks.doc: One call of a system body, once per run of the schedule, or once per slice when the system is per_entity. A failure is carried to the caller of run, which fails with it; the rest of the wave still runs, and no later wave starts.

lanes.name: ctx
lanes.doc: The body's only doorway to component memory for this call.

callbacks.name: ke_schedule_condition_fn
callbacks.doc: Whether a system runs in this run of its schedule; asked once per run, before the first wave, on the thread that called run. A failure fails the run before any wave starts.
